doc: Float32 values of 1e30 and -3e29 (huge, negative, mixed): the float32 row sums stay finite (32 x 1e30 < 3.4e38) and the weighted mean is about 3.5e29. Tolerance is the golden float32 default (rtol 1e-5): the huge magnitude makes the absolute error large, the relative one not. Arguments: a, the field (h, w), north-up. Weights: c_i = cos(lat_i) at the cell centres of grid_lonlat(w, h), row i at lat_i = 90 deg - (i + 0.5) 180 deg / h (row 0 is north, float64 radians pi/2 - (i + 0.5) pi / h); result = sum_i(mean_j a[i, j] c_i) / sum_i c_i, a float64 scalar stored as a one-element array. The row mean runs in the dtype of a (float32 rows are averaged in float32, numpy pairwise summation), the weighting in float64. Measured: promoting the float32 inputs to float64 changes the output by at most 0; one-ulp nudges of every float input and parameter change it by at most 1.7e+22 (worst of 6 random trials); the tolerance is about 2e2x the larger of the two spreads.
